Create an Unregulated-to-Regulated Inflow Transformation Function

Source: R/unreg_reg_transform.R
unreg_reg_transform.Rd

Constructs a function that transforms unregulated inflow values to corresponding regulated inflow values using linear interpolation. By default, input values outside the range of the supplied unregulated inflows are returned unchanged.

Usage

unreg_reg_transform(unreg_inflow, reg_inflow, extend = TRUE)

Arguments

unreg_inflow

Numeric vector of unregulated inflow values. Values should represent the independent variable for the interpolation.

reg_inflow

Numeric vector of regulated inflow values corresponding element-wise to unreg_inflow.

extend

Logical; if TRUE (default), values passed to the returned function that fall outside the observed range of unreg_inflow are returned unchanged. If FALSE, out-of-range values return NA.

Value

A function accepting a numeric vector x and returning a numeric vector of interpolated regulated inflow values.

Details

The transformation uses stats::approxfun() with rule = 1, which produces NA for values outside the interpolation range. When extend = TRUE, those out-of-range values are replaced with their original input values rather than extrapolated.

Missing values in x are preserved as NA. The minimum and maximum interpolation bounds are calculated with missing values removed from unreg_inflow.

Examples

unreg_inflow <- c(0, 100, 200, 300)
reg_inflow <- c(0, 90, 170, 240)

transform_inflow <- unreg_reg_transform(unreg_inflow, reg_inflow)

# Interpolated value
transform_inflow(150)
#> [1] 130

# Out-of-range values are unchanged when extend = TRUE
transform_inflow(c(-10, 50, 350))
#> [1] -10  45 350

# Out-of-range values return NA when extend = FALSE
strict_transform <- unreg_reg_transform(
  unreg_inflow,
  reg_inflow,
  extend = FALSE
)
strict_transform(c(-10, 50, 350))
#> [1] NA 45 NA
